narration.text: That's the class. Now put the same slice against the names near the top of the opening chart, full catalogs, everything at full credit. Travis Scott, sixty-seven billion. Kendrick, fifty-seven. Post Malone, fifty-six. Future, fifty-four. The slice clears every one of them.

acceptableDurationSeconds.note: Descriptive. Corpus median 9.0s, p75 14.0s. Never a cap: the evidence sets the length.

internalChangeBudget.note: Advisory. May suggest splitting a unit, but never rejects a candidate and never forces a split. Overridden whenever the content needs the time.

contract.takeaway: His lead-credit slice alone beats four full catalogs from the top of the chart.

claims.text: Travis Scott's full catalog is 67 billion.
Kendrick Lamar is 57 billion, Post Malone 56, Future 54.
His lead-credit slice exceeds every one of them.

requiredMedia.contentRequirement: Verified full-catalog totals for the four peers and the lead-credit slice for the subject, on one fixed scale.
Approved portraits for the four named peers.

visualEvents.triggerPhrase: The slice clears every one of them
visualEvents.description: The subject's slice is shown above all four.
visualEvents.matchedTranscript: The slice clears every one of them.

prohibitions.prohibition: Do not compare full catalog against full catalog.
prohibitions.reason: The claim is a partial slice against complete catalogs. Losing that asymmetry loses the point.

prohibitions.prohibition: Do not rescale to the supplied range.
prohibitions.reason: User ruling on this passage: the third candidate should have been the 3D scatter, which carries the gap as distance.

successConditions: The asymmetry between a slice and four full catalogs is explicit.
failureConditions: The slice is presented as a full catalog.
The four peers are not individually identified.
